messages:
lina: Heads-up — seeing sustained queue depth and token wait times on shared-pool-us-west for the last 2h. 95th gen latency up ~2.8x. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/in/boards/GPUSat
ben: I also saw a big bump around 13:12. Two tenants (arbor, quill) spiked concurrent short-runs. KV cache miss rate went up too.
carla: Agree. I think noisy-neighbor from many small, high-concurrency jobs. Proposal: a 'soft-fence' admission layer — per-tenant token bucket + elastic borrow from idle pool with penalty decay.
ben: Sketch config? want something we can simulate quickly.
carla: Example policy (pseudo):
```
admission_policy:
  tenants:
    - id: arbor
      base_tokens: 40
      max_burst: 120
      decay_seconds: 300
    - id: default
      base_tokens: 10
  global_idle_pool: 500
  borrow_penalty: 0.25  # apply holdback when borrowing
```
carla: Idea is to allow short bursts but apply soft-muting if tenant borrows repeatedly (drop priority not requests).
devops-bot: autoscaler: scaling events suppressed while pool borrowing > 0.75 for >10m.
erin: How do we keep fairness? This could still favor big tenants with steady traffic.
frank: Weight-based shares on top of token buckets. Each tenant gets share = committed_capacity * weight, weight defaults to 1 but can be set for enterprise customers.
frank: Also propose sampled admission: we only enforce strict drops if queue depth > Q_high, otherwise throttle by delaying scheduling (100-500ms backoff) to keep latency bounded.
maya: Rollout plan: implement in admission-proxy behind feature flag. Canary on us-west1-rack-3 for 48h, compare per-tenant tail latency and OOM rates.
ben: Telemetry we need: per-tenant queue depth, borrow_count, penalized_seconds, KV hitrate, gen_p95. Add alert if penalized_seconds > 30% for top 10 tenants.
carla: Also add a low-traffic protection rule: if tenant qps < 5/min then exempt from borrow penalties for 1h to avoid punishing small apps.
lina: Cost angle — borrowing idle pool reduces immediate scale-ups but may increase token-hours. We should simulate cost vs SLA impact for a week of traces.
erin: Can we do an offline sim on last 30 days and publish numbers? I can run sims if I get the model of concurrent job sizes.
ben: I'll export traces. Putting them in s3://redwood-sim/soft-fence/2055-05-01
frank: Fallback behavior: if penalized and still over limit, route new requests to a cheaper quantized variant or queued response with ETA header.
carla: Implementation notes: admission-proxy needs tenant score, borrow ledger (redis), and a small ML model to predict short vs long-run (heuristic ok initially).
maya: Obs: ensure the canary doesn't auto-evict dedicated customers. Add label exclude:dedi=true
lina: Proposed timeline: week0 implement feature-flag + sim, week1 canary, week2 evaluate and extend region.
erin: :thumbsup: Sounds reasonable. I'll own the sim and dashboard widgets.
ben: I'll own the export and the canary infra.
carla: I'll PR admission-proxy patch and include config validator + unit tests.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary pipeline created: pipeline/soft-fence-canary (us-west1-rack-3)
lina: Thanks all — let's sync in weekly eng-platform standup. If anyone sees regressions after canary, ping #oncall immediately.
notes: This thread discusses implementing a soft-fencing admission control to mitigate noisy tenants in the shared GPU pool. Contains a config sketch, rollout plan, metrics to monitor, and owners for sim and canary.
